item: An encrypted working copy keeps its rows out of temp files during a merge
key_paths: src/backup/merge.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/locales/*.json; src/monitoring/merge_diag.py; tests/test_merge_encrypted_temp.py; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md
summary: merge_corpus set temp_store=FILE on every working copy; on an ENCRYPTED one the sorter's spill file (CREATE INDEX, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, UNION, IN-subqueries) is written through the VFS below the codec, so row text reached the temp directory in the clear (WAL's reading, reproduced: FILE leaks, MEMORY opens no row-holding temp file). An encrypted working copy now holds temp structures in MEMORY and a plain one keeps FILE; its need is measured (the windowed steps +41 to +64 MB of peak RSS, bounded by the byte-denominated window; the three unwindowed whole-source grouping steps 67 to 147 B per incoming row, which grow with the corpus) and an encrypted merge asks first for twice the window plus the largest grouping step for the incoming rows counted from the staged file plus the memory guard's floor of available memory, refusing before any row moves with a fixed sentence the page reads into a keyed frame (x12); an unreadable figure never refuses and a plain store is never gated. Every statement the merge runs on that copy was walked; the other merge connections never set temp_store (driver default MEMORY) and merge_diag's probe sorts synthetic rows. Tests pin MEMORY on encrypted, FILE on plain, the gate (need, incoming rows, largest-not-sum, floor, unreadable, plain exempt, refusal writes nothing), the /proc spill control and the page frame; every mutant is killed.
